findings.title: Duplicate keyword `sort_keys` raises TypeError when caller passes `sort_keys`
findings.explanation: end_serialization() does `yaml.dump(..., sort_keys=False, **self.options)`. findings.title: Implicit minimum PyYAML bump to ≥5.1 not documented

review.summary: Breaking signature change (`**hints` -> `*, instance`) and dropped `instance` hint handling for custom prefetches breaks backward compatibility and multi-db routing.

findings.title: Breaking public API: get_queryset() now requires keyword-only `instance`
findings.explanation: Old code was `def get_queryset(self, **hints)` so `desc.get_queryset()` or `desc.get_queryset(instance=obj)` and `desc.get_queryset(db='other')` worked and arbitrary hints were forwarded to `db_manager(hints=hints)`. New code `def get_queryset(self, *, instance)` makes any call without `instance=` raise TypeError, and any existing subclass overriding `def get_queryset(self, **hints)` that is instantiated via the framework will now be called as `get_queryset(instance=inst)` – which still collects in `**hints` but internal callers that expect to pass through extra hints lose them (hardcoded `hints={"instance": instance}`). This breaks external descriptors (e.g. custom ForeignObject subclasses in tests/foreign_object) and any third-party code inspecting/calling the descriptor directly. Should retain backwards-compat shim e.g. `def get_queryset(self, instance=None, **hints)` merging hints.

findings.title: Missing instance hint when `querysets` supplied in get_prefetch_querysets()
findings.explanation: Previously: `queryset = querysets[0] if querysets else self.get_queryset(); queryset._add_hints(instance=instances[0])` – hint was added regardless of source. Now: `queryset = querysets[0] if querysets else self.get_queryset(instance=instances[0])` with no following `_add_hints`. When a user supplies `Prefetch('field', queryset=custom_qs)` the queryset loses the `instance` hint needed for `router.db_for_read(..., instance=...)`. Other managers (ReverseManyToOneDescriptor, ManyToMany) still do `queryset._add_hints(...)` after the ternary. Fix: add branch that calls `_add_hints` for the custom-queryset case.

findings.title: Same breaking signature and hint loss on ReverseOneToOneDescriptor
findings.explanation: Identical issue as ForwardManyToOneDescriptor at line 169/174 applies to ReverseOneToOneDescriptor.get_queryset()/get_prefetch_querysets() at 462/467: API break and omitted `_add_hints` for provided querysets.

findings.title: Descending "-field" ordering crashes count()
findings.explanation: self.order_by stores strings with leading "-" (add_ordering keeps dash). Property does F(order_by).resolve_expression(q) without stripping direction, so "-id" -> F("-id").resolve_ref tries to resolve field "-id" and raises FieldError. findings.title: group_by==True assumed always subset of order_by
findings.explanation: Property returns True when self.group_by is True, claiming order_by is necessarily subset of auto-generated model-field grouping. findings.title: OrderBy/F expression handling breaks subset check

review.summary: Optimization bypasses regex for converter-less routes but breaks lazy-translated (`gettext_lazy`) RoutePattern matches: non-endpoint `path.startswith(self._route)` / `removeprefix` pass a Promise to `str` C-API (`TypeError`) and don't evaluate per-language value correctly, while endpoint equality is fragile versus explicit `str()` handling.

findings.title: Lazy-translated RoutePattern crashes / mismatches
findings.explanation: For `RoutePattern("foo/" or _("translated/"))` with `converters=={}` the new fast-path does `path.startswith(self._route)` and `path.removeprefix(self._route)`. `self._route` may be a `Promise` (result of `gettext_lazy`). `str.startswith()`/`removeprefix()` require `str`/tuple, not `Promise`, raising `TypeError: startswith first arg must be str or a tuple of str, not __proxy__` for i18n includes (`path(_("translated/"), include(...))`, `_is_endpoint=False`). Even where `self._route == path` happens to work via `Promise.__eq__`, the prefix branch does not delegate to the proxy (receiver is the plain `path` string). It should evaluate the current translation once via `route = str(self._route)` and then do `route == path` / `path.startswith(route)` / `path[len(route):]` to mirror the per-language regex compilation (`LocaleRegexRouteDescriptor` uses `str(self._route)` + `get_language()`).

findings.title: Endpoint fast-path should use translated string
findings.explanation: `if self._route == path` relies on `Promise.__eq__` only when left is the proxy. While it currently succeeds for endpoint views (`is_endpoint=True`), it is asymmetric and inconsistent with the regex path which uses `str(self._route)` for the active language. Use `str(self._route) == path` (and similarly for the prefix case) to guarantee correct language-aware matching.

findings.title: Same missing wiring for YAxis plus stale width logic interaction
findings.explanation: YAxisProps mirrors XAxisProps with fontSize/letterSpacing but YAxisSettingsDispatcher never persists them. Even if passed via ...allOtherProps, CartesianAxisComponent reads its own useState fontSize/letterSpacing from window.getComputedStyle and overwrites any explicit value on layerRef, so the prop cannot override DOM measurement as intended.

findings.explanation: Old hooks called selectTicksOfAxis(state, type, id, isPanorama). New selectRenderedTicksOfAxis(state,type,id) is keyed only by (type,id) and ignores PanoramaContext. Main chart and Brush panorama both mount CartesianAxis with same axisId=0 and report via RenderedTicksReporter to the same slice key, racing and overwriting each other. useXAxisInverseTickSnapScale/useYAxisInverseTickSnapScale now snap to main-chart ticks even when called inside <Brush> panorama, regressing brush interaction.

findings.title: useXAxisTicks/useYAxisTicks now async and changes return shape

First render therefore returns undefined and later renders return a filtered subset after overlap culling; code expecting immediate full tick list or accessing payload/tickCoord breaks, and existing selectors/tests had to bump call counts 2→3 for the extra dispatch cycle.

findings.title: RenderedTicksReporter discards useful fields and dispatches on every identity change
findings.explanation: Mapping to {value,coordinate,offset,index} drops payload, tickCoord, tickSize, isShow that callers of CartesianTickItem may rely on. review.summary: Right-click panning blocks to open the menu on release but the camera only jumps once: the incremental panning loop is gated on `isPointing` which is never set for the right-button path, so drags stall after the drag-threshold. Synthetic `contextmenu` dispatched as `PointerEvent` and pointer-capture transfer between MenuClickCapture and canvas are also fragile.

findings.title: Incremental right-click panning never runs – gated on `isPointing`
findings.explanation: `pointer_down` for button 2 with `rightClickPanning` sets `isRightPointing` but not `isPointing`. `pointer_move` first transitions to `isPanning` with a one-shot `origin→current` delta then returns. The continuation block is `if (inputs.getIsPanning() && inputs.getIsPointing())` – false for right-drag (comment claims it handles right-click). Subsequent moves fall through with no camera update, so the viewport only jumps once instead of following the drag.

findings.title: Pointer capture transferred to canvas leaks/steals moves from MenuClickCapture
findings.explanation: `handlePointerDown` does `setPointerCapture(menuDiv)` then `canvasEvents.onPointerDown({currentTarget:canvas})` which internally `setPointerCapture(canvas)`. Per spec only one element can capture a pointer – the second call releases capture from the menu div. Later moves/ups then target the canvas (or are handled by the body listener) while `handlePointerMove/Up` on the capture overlay stop firing, leaving the canvas capture unreleased on menu-overlay pan.

findings.title: Synthetic contextmenu dispatched as PointerEvent
findings.explanation: Both canvas and menu-overlay paths do `new PointerEvent('contextmenu',…)`. `contextmenu` is a MouseEvent; using PointerEvent is non-standard and may not propagate to Radix/listeners expecting MouseEvent properties in some browsers. Use `new MouseEvent('contextmenu',…)` with `bubbles:true`.

review.summary: PR claims minor bugfixes but introduces mutating Vec methods, ineffective Rectangle SVG fix, and breaking API privatization that will break existing consumers.

findings.title: Vec.uni() instance now mutates caller instead of returning new Vec
findings.explanation: Old instance `uni()` delegated to `Vec.Uni(this)` which returns a new Vec (pure). New implementation divides `this` in place (`this.x/=l`). Any caller doing `const u = a.uni(); // expect a unchanged` or chaining `Vec.Sub(a,b).uni()` that relied on Sub's result being disposable but later reused `a` will now see `a` mutated. Also breaks `tan()` which now does `this.sub(V).uni()` mutating the receiver instead of pure `Vec.Tan(this,V)`.

findings.title: Vec.toFixed() instance now mutates geometry vectors
findings.explanation: Old `toFixed()` returned `Vec.ToFixed(this)` (new Vec). New mutates `this` via `toFixed(this.x)`. Call sites like `Edge2d.getSvgPathData(): start.toFixed()` and `Arc2d/CubicBezier` now permanently round the stored geometry points (`_start`, `_a`, etc.) to 2-decimal precision on first SVG export, corrupting hit-testing and future renders.

findings.title: Vec.tan() now mutates receiver
findings.explanation: Previously `tan(V)` returned `Vec.Tan(this,V)` (pure, creates new Vec). Now `return this.sub(V).uni()` mutates `this` in place. Callers expecting non-mutating tangent (e.g., `pos.tan(other)` preserving `pos`) will have `pos` overwritten with direction.

findings.title: Rectangle SVG negative-zero fix is ineffective
findings.explanation: `getSvgPathData` destructures `{_x:x,_y:y,_w:w,_h:h}=this` before calling `this.negativeZeroFix()`, so the returned string `M${x},${y} h${w}...` still contains `-0` (or un-fixed values). Fix must run before destructuring or use `this._x` directly after fixing.

findings.title: New throws on <2 points break backward compat
findings.explanation: Constructor now throws if `points.length < 2` (and `Polygon2d` <3). Previously callers could construct degenerate geometry (used during shape creation/interpolation). This is a runtime regression – existing shapes or tests passing empty/singleton arrays will now crash instead of producing empty geometry.

findings.title: Public geometry fields made private without replacement
findings.explanation: All public fields (`_center,radius,start,end,largeArcFlag,sweepFlag,measure,angleStart/End` and equivalents in Circle2d, Edge2d, Rectangle2d, Stadium2d, Ellipse2d, etc.) were changed to `private _*`. They were part of public exports (api-report.md) – external code/tests accessing `rect.w`/`circle.radius`/`edge.start` etc. now gets undefined at runtime and TypeScript errors. This is an unintended breaking API change for a bugfix PR.

review.summary: PR expands `EditorOptions.element` typing to `Element|{mount}|callback|null` and rewrites React/Vue adapters to move `editor.view.dom` directly, but `Editor.mount/createView` was not updated to handle the new union so the promised API crashes, and the adapter changes introduce `view.dom` access via a throwing proxy when the view is not mounted/destroyed.

findings.title: New `element` union not implemented in `mount`/`createView`
findings.explanation: Types now advertises `{mount: HTMLElement}` and `(el)=>void` as valid `element` values (changeset hip-windows-retire.md) but `mount(el)` and `createView(element)` still do `new EditorView(element,...)` directly. Passing the new shapes will throw/type-error at runtime; docs promise behavior that does not exist.

findings.title: Type over-promises mounting modes
findings.explanation: Changing `element: Element|null` to `Element|{mount:HTMLElement}|((editor:HTMLElement)=>void)|null` widens the public API without runtime support. Existing `Element|null` callers unaffected, but any consumer following the new docs/changelog will hit a crash in core.

findings.title: `editor.view.dom` access can throw when view unavailable
findings.explanation: When unmounted/destroyed `editor.view` is a Proxy that throws on unknown properties like `dom`. New code does `element.append(editor.view.dom)` and `editor.view.dom?.firstChild` without guarding `isDestroyed`/availability. Old code used `editor.options.element` which is always safe. This crashes e.g. componentWillUnmount after external destroy.

findings.title: Guard changed from wrapper child to content child
findings.explanation: Old guard `!editor.options.element?.firstChild` checked whether the mount wrapper contains the ProseMirror view (i.e., view was actually attached). New guard `!editor.view.dom?.firstChild` checks whether the editable content itself has a child (first paragraph/text). For an empty doc or a view moved/destroyed the conditions differ, causing missed re-parenting or false early-return.

findings.title: Same throwing `view.dom` access in Vue 2 adapter
findings.explanation: Inside `$nextTick` handler and `beforeDestroy`, new code accesses `editor.view.dom?.firstChild` and `element.append(editor.view.dom)`. If the tick fires after destroy/unmount, the Proxy throws instead of safely no-oping via `options.element`.

findings.title: Same throwing `view.dom` access in Vue 3 adapter
findings.explanation: `watchEffect` nextTick callback and teardown now depend on `editor.view.dom`. Same proxy-throw regression as React/Vue2; previously guarded by `editor.options.element`.

findings.title: Clone/replace logic now clones `view.dom` not wrapper and can throw
findings.explanation: Was `nodes = options.element` (wrapper) cloned and replaced in its parent to preserve visible HTML after destroy. Now `nodes = view.dom` so only inner ProseMirror node is cloned and replaced inside the wrapper, changing DOM output and leaving wrapper semantics different. Also `editor.value?.view.dom` throws when view not yet mounted/destroyed (proxy), whereas `options.element` was safe optional chain.

AstPath.previous/next can be null for whitespace at document boundaries (and defensively elsewhere – isBreakable/lineBreakCanBeConvertedToSpace both guard with !previous||!next). A text starting/ending with an ambiguous '\n' (previous or next null, other side isCJ true) will throw Cannot read properties of null. Fix: use previous?.kind / next?.kind and handle null.

findings.title: isLineBreakAmbiguous applied to wrong path for link-reference content

Should bypass the ambiguous-preserve logic when isLink===true or only evaluate it for real whitespace nodes (printWhitespaceNode).

review.summary: SSR scope cleanup is correct for isolated apps but introduces error-masking in `renderToString` and retains the underlying cross-request race via shared `appContext.provides`.

findings.title: finally masking original render error
findings.explanation: `cleanupContext` throws first dispose error from `finally{}`. If `renderComponentVNode`/`unrollBuffer`/`resolveTeleports` rejected and a `onScopeDispose`/`unwatch` also throws, JS `finally` semantics discard the original render failure. `renderToSimpleStream` preserves the original error via try/catch around `finalize()`, but `renderToString` does not, losing diagnostics.

findings.title: scope ownership tied to mutable appContext.provides
findings.explanation: Scopes are registered via `instance.appContext.provides[ssrContextKey]`. `input.provide()` mutates the single `appContext.provides` object, so two concurrent `renderToString`/`renderToStream` calls reusing the same `App` instance race: the second `provide` overwrites the first, and any child `createComponentInstance` after an async `setup` gap reads the latest value and pushes its `instance.scope` onto the wrong `SSRContext.__instanceScopes`. Separate apps (as in the added test) work, but same-app concurrency leaks/double-frees.

findings.title: cleanup leaves stale provide reference
findings.explanation: `cleanupContext` clears array lengths but never removes the `ssrContextKey` provide from `appContext.provides`. Reusing an `App` sequentially keeps a live reference to the previous `SSRContext` (with `teleports`/`__instanceScopes`) until overwritten, retaining memory and potentially exposing stale teleports on next render if provide is read before overwrite.

findings.title: Over-aggressive stripping for TS root loses real code
findings.explanation: When `ast.type ∈ TS_NODE_TYPES` the code skips the whole `leadingText` before the first identifier and the whole `trailingText` after the last (`!(isTSNode&&i===0)` and `&&!isTSNode`). Those are discarded. Old code leaked ` as string` but preserved the prefix; new code silently changes semantics to `_ctx.foo`. Same for first/last `(`/`)` grouping that should be kept.

findings.title: Type casts in non-root position still leak into JS output
findings.explanation: `isTSNode` is only checked against the top-level `ast.type`. Expressions where a cast is inside another expr still emit TS syntax: `foo as number + bar` → gap ` as number + ` → `_ctx.foo as number + _ctx.bar`; `(foo as any).bar`, `(foo as any)(e)`, `x ? y as T : z`, `fn(a as string,b)` all leak. `walkIdentifiers` correctly ignores type ids, but `processExpression` re-inserts the raw slice between ids unchanged. Parser wrapping/Program vs Expression differences (asRawStatements/asParams, ParenthesizedExpression) make the `ast.type` check brittle and ineffective for those cases.

review.summary: Anchor.handleScrollTo never cancels the previous animation because activeLinkRef is updated before the comparison, and it still starts a new animation on same-link clicks; the cancelled animation also never clears animating.current and has no unmount cleanup, permanently disabling scroll handling.

findings.title: Cancellation check dead due to setCurrentActiveLink ordering
findings.explanation: handleScrollTo calls setCurrentActiveLink(link) on line 272 which sets activeLinkRef.current = link, then checks animating.current && activeLinkRef.current !== link on line 282. After the update the condition is always false for normal links (only true when getCurrentAnchor remaps), so rapid clicks on different anchors never cancel the previous raf loop. Two concurrent scrollTo loops fight for window.scrollTo and final Y is non-deterministic.

findings.title: Same-link click during animation still starts duplicate scrollTo
findings.explanation: The intended fix (and new test 'should not scroll when clicking the same active link') requires an early-return when activeLinkRef.current === link while animating. Current code only cancels when different, otherwise falls through to compute y and call scrollTo again, overwriting scrollRequestId without cancelling the prior raf. Test expectation fails and overlapping animations conflict.

findings.title: animating flag leaked after cancel and no unmount cleanup
findings.explanation: scrollTo cancel (raf.cancel) prevents the callback that does animating.current=false from ever running. When the previous animation is cancelled and replaced, animating stays true until next completes - benign - but if component unmounts mid-animation there is no effect cleanup that calls scrollRequestId.current?.(). handleScroll is gated by animating.current, so it remains blocked forever and the outstanding raf leaks. The test 'properly cleanup' asserts nothing because cleanup was not implemented.

findings.title: Return-type changed to cancel function without updating callers/mocks
findings.explanation: scrollTo previously returned void, now returns () => void. Existing mocks like components/table/__tests__/Table.pagination.test.tsx use mockReturnValue(null) assuming void; with strict types this leaks null into scrollRequestId.current and optional chaining hides errors. More importantly external users of scrollTo that ignored return now silently hold no way to clean up, and types/docs not updated.

review.summary: Fix correctly resets clickedRef for Popconfirm emitEvent path but introduces a new console.error/swallow contract change and leaves the two Modal paths (actionFn(close) and actionFn()) unprotected, so synchronous throws there still leave clickedRef stuck and retry impossible.

findings.title: Only emitEvent branch handles sync throw; Modal branches still deadlock
findings.explanation: The new try/catch wraps only `if (emitEvent) actionFn(e)`. The `else if (actionFn.length) actionFn(close)` and `else actionFn()` paths (used by Modal ConfirmOkBtn/ConfirmCancelBtn) still call actionFn without try/catch. If they throw synchronously, `clickedRef.current = false` on line 125 is never reached (exception before it) and the `else` branch never resets clickedRef at all, so subsequent clicks are ignored exactly like the original Popconfirm bug. Fix needs try/catch around those calls too.

findings.title: Sync error is swallowed and console.error changes public API contract
findings.explanation: Previously a synchronous throw escaped onClick (visible to ErrorBoundaries/window.onerror). Now it is caught, `clickedRef` reset, then swallowed with `console.error('Error in actionFn:', error)` unless isSilent. Popconfirm never passes isSilent so it always logs. This pollutes production consoles, mismatches async path which does `return Promise.reject(e)` unless silent, and hides errors from callers expecting propagation. Should reset clickedRef then re-throw or respect existing isSilent semantics without introducing unconditional console.error.

findings.title: "Silent mode" test does not actually exercise silent mode
findings.explanation: Test titled 'should not log error when onConfirm throws error in silent mode' renders Popconfirm without providing isSilent (ActionButton uses undefined => !isSilent?.() is true) and then asserts consoleError was called, opposite of title. review.summary: Pickle round-trip is implemented by storing `module_path` and re-importing, but `_reconstruct` validates "points to a Task instance" only via catching `AttributeError` on `.func`, which can be bypassed by any importable object that happens to have a `.func` attribute pointing to an allowed function.

findings.title: _reconstruct does not verify Task type
findings.explanation: `_reconstruct` does `func = import_string(func_path); kwargs['func'] = func.func` inside try/except ImportError,AttributeError. If `func_path` imports an object that is not a Task but has a `.func` attribute (many decorators/wrappers, or attacker-controlled module), `func.func` succeeds and an arbitrary callable is wrapped as Task. The subsequent `validate_task` only checks `is_module_level_function` (e.g. subprocess.run is considered valid), so an attacker-controlled pickle payload could synthesize a Task for a non-task function. Should explicitly check `isinstance(func, Task)` (or `type(func) is Task`/subclass) and raise ValueError otherwise.

findings.title: _reconstruct mutates caller dict and leaks KeyError
findings.explanation: `kwargs['func'] = func.func` mutates the dict passed to `__reduce__`/tests. Also `kwargs['func']` lookup raises raw KeyError if 'func' missing from crafted pickle, instead of the intended ValueError("Expected ... to point to a Task instance."). Copy the dict before mutating and validate key presence.

findings.title: TaskResult pickling relies on transitive dataclass pickle
findings.explanation: Docs claim TaskResult is picklable but no __reduce__/__getstate__ is added. It works only because Task is now picklable and TaskResult is a frozen-slots dataclass whose auto pickle bypasses __post_init__ normalize_json. This is fragile and test `test_pickle_task_result` only covers READY result with _return_value=None; a SUCCESSFUL/FAILED result with mutated attributes (_return_value, enqueued_at via object.__setattr__) should have an explicit test to ensure full state round-trips.

review.summary: Fix correctly addresses stale-branch case but introduces an always-true filter, unbounded retention of created effects, and rescheduling into later batches.

findings.title: current_unequal filter compares value to source identity
findings.explanation: `[...batch.current.keys()].filter(c=> this.current.has(c) ? this.current.get(c)[0] !== c : true)` compares the stored batch value to the source object `c` itself, so `!== c` is almost always true. Intended check is whether `this` and `batch` disagree on value, e.g. `this.current.get(c)[0] !== batch.current.get(c)[0]`. As written the filter is a no-op and causes over-scheduling into every batch.

findings.title: #new_effects never cleared — memory leak and duplicate rescheduling
findings.explanation: `#new_effects` is appended to in `register_created_effect()` but never cleared after `#commit()` (and `discard()` does not clear it). The committing Batch retains references to all effects it created forever, and if the same Batch participates in multiple commit traversals the same effects are re-evaluated repeatedly.

review.summary: Change adds visual clipping and a domain-guard to hide the active dot, but the guard incorrectly ties tooltip visibility to the computed tooltip-axis domain and breaks keyboard/fallback behavior, and clipping is conditional on `needClip`.

findings.title: Domain guard only checks one axis and mis-handles allowDataOverflow
findings.explanation: `isValueWithinDomain` is only evaluated against `selectTooltipAxisDomain`/`selectTooltipAxisDataKey`. Points that are outside the Y domain (or both axes) but inside the X domain still pass and the active dot can still be drawn outside the plot. More critically the guard runs against the final computed domain (`combineAxisDomain`), which expands the user domain when `allowDataOverflow===false` (via `extendDomain`). `combineActiveTooltipIndex` therefore returns non-null when overflow is disabled, while `test/component/Tooltip/ActiveDot.spec.tsx:286` expects suppression for both true/false. In practice with `allowDataOverflow=false` the domain `[1.01,1.15]` is expanded to include the data `[0.9,1.3]` – tooltip should remain visible per Recharts contract, but the new `selectIsTooltipActive`/`selectActiveTooltipIndex` wiring hides it, breaking existing behavior; with `allowDataOverflow=true` the intended suppression works but the test cannot pass for both branches.

findings.title: Active-dot clipping only when needClip, leaves hole when domain guard fails
findings.explanation: `activePointsClipPath` is `undefined` when `needClip===false` (both axes `allowDataOverflow===false`). If `combineActiveTooltipIndex` fails to suppress (e.g. overflow-disabled expanded domain case above) the active dot is rendered without any `clipPath` and can appear outside the graph. Same pattern in `src/cartesian/Area.tsx:662`. Fix should clip unconditionally (or via Y/X separately) or ensure the domain guard is reliable.

findings.title: Keyboard navigation can step into out-of-domain index and get stuck
findings.explanation: `resolvedIndex` now respects the domain guard, but `nextIndex` is validated only against `tooltipTicks.length`. Arrow navigation can move from a valid index to an index whose datum is outside `selectTooltipAxisDomain`; the next render then yields `null` active index and the following Arrow press exits early (`!Number.isFinite(currentIndex) || currentIndex<0`) leaving the keyboard interaction stranded on an invisible/inactive index. Should validate `chartData[nextIndex]` against the domain before dispatching.

findings.title: selectIsTooltipActive API change from active-flag to activeIndex-null coupling
findings.explanation: Changed from `{isActive: tooltipInteractionState.active}` to `active && activeIndex!=null`. Callers that relied on `isActive` independent of data validity (e.g. item hover, custom tooltip triggers) now see `isActive=false` when the clamped index maps to an out-of-domain datum, changing public selector semantics and tooltip/cursor visibility.

review.summary: PR correctly awaits async/blocked dependencies for bindings, static props and style directives, and fixes hydration end-marker rewind. No crashing regressions observed; remaining gaps are narrow edge-cases.

findings.title: Functional binding visit skips function scope
findings.explanation: For `bind:value={get,set}` where get/set are ArrowFunctionExpressions, the code visits only `get.body`/`set.body` to avoid resetting `context.state.expression`. This bypasses creation of the arrow-function scope, so a setter parameter like `v => value = v` that shadows an outer state variable `v` with a blocker will be treated as a reference to the outer `v`, incorrectly adding its blocker/dependencies. Old code ignored functional bindings entirely, so this is an improvement but still mishandles shadowing. Affects only names colliding shadowing cases.

findings.title: Spread path for BindDirective misses blocker tracking
findings.explanation: `build_element_attributes` now calls `transform(…, attribute.metadata.expression)` for BindDirective so server async-blockers are recorded. The spread-object path `build_spread_object` (used when an element has `...spread`) still does `context.visit(attribute.expression)` without `transform`/`check_blockers` for `BindDirective`. A `<div {...spread} bind:value={asyncVar}>` that goes through spread handling would therefore not contribute its blocker to `PromiseOptimiser`, breaking the async fix for that less common path.

findings.title: Shorthand style-directive spread case ignores blockers
findings.explanation: In `prepare_element_spread` shorthand branches `directive.value===true ? b.id(name)` and `build_attr_style`/`build_attr_class` for spread cases do not wrap via `transform`. If a spread-element uses shorthand `style:color` where the implicit binding has a blocker, no blocker is registered, unlike the non-spread path fixed in `BuildStyleDirective/RegularElement`. Benign for typical templates.

review.summary: Fix correctly batches record-scope updates to avoid SQLite live-cursor revisits and does the same for the arrow ExtractBindings storage migration; behavior is preserved and regression tests verify exactly-once execution.

findings.title: Final document-scope cleanup still mutates during iteration
findings.explanation: The loop `for (const [id, state] of storage.entries()) { if (scope !== 'document') storage.delete(id) }` deletes while iterating a live SQLite cursor. Like the record-migration bug this PR fixes, SQLite docs say modifying a table during an active SELECT is undefined and can skip rows, leaving non-document legacy records undeleted. Should collect ids first then delete, consistent with the record-migration fix.

findings.title: Other storage-scope migrations still delete during live iteration
findings.explanation: Three storage migrations (RemoveCodeAndIconShapeTypes, RemoveTLUserAndPresenceAndAddPointer, RemoveUserDocument) iterate `storage.entries()` and call `storage.delete(id)` inside the loop. Same live-iterator hazard as the fixed arrow migration exists here; a batched-collect-then-delete pattern would make them safe for SQLiteSyncStorage. Low risk because they are old retroactive:false migrations, but inconsistent with the new best-practice established by this PR.
